use_case_name: Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to define reference points and geometric areas (specifically slaved points and areas) in relation to a Related TN.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.3.1.3 header 'SLAVED POINTS AND AREAS' and paragraph a

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section explicitly describes the process of defining 'Slaved Points and Areas', which aligns with the use case goal of defining reference points and geometric areas.

evidence_cards.content: The primary actor (C2 JU) aims to report specific points, lines, or areas immediately without awaiting the next periodic update by transmitting a J7.1 Data Update Request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the high-level objective of immediate reporting for specific geospatial data elements.

evidence_cards.content: The goal is to initiate or terminate force tell alerts and emergency alerts on reference points, lines, areas, and tracks by setting appropriate indicator fields (FT IND, EMG IND) in J3.x messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This claim defines the high-level objective of the use case regarding alert management for geospatial entities.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.0 message is used to exchange tactical information about geographic references such as waypoints, Combat Air Patrol (CAP) stations, and Forward Edge of the Battle Area (FEBA).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the high-level objective of defining reference points and geometric areas for tactical information exchange, which aligns with the use case goal.

evidence_cards.content: The primary actor (C2 JU) defines reference points and geometric areas by specifying parameters such as Point Type, Line and Point Amplification, Delta Latitude/Longitude, and Slaved Indicators to establish positions relative to a Related TN.

Page 4-163 paragraph c and section 4.4.3.1.3; Page 4-164 section 4.4.3.1.4

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the high-level objective of the use case: defining specific types of points (slaved, moving) and areas (corridors, LLTRs, ASW AOPs) using the defined message fields.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.0 Reference Point message is used to report the actual or expected Impact Point of a ballistic missile.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific objective of reporting impact points, which constitutes the goal for defining reference points in this context.

evidence_cards.content: Emergency alerts are not used on reference points, lines, or areas.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement directly addresses the scope and limitations of alert usage for reference points and geometric areas, which is central to defining the goal of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a necessary state that must hold before the C2 JU assumes R2 of an IU and reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG, which aligns with defining reference points in relation to a Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: For slaved points, a 'Related TN' must exist to serve as the reference position.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the dependency on an external entity (Related TN) before a slaved point can be defined.

evidence_cards.content: For slaved points, the system must have established Delta Latitude and 1/Delta Longitude values relative to the Related TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific geometric data required to establish the constant bearing and range of the slaved point.

evidence_cards.content: For non-slaved moving points, Course and Speed information must be available and set to values other than 'No Statement'.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the necessary kinematic data state required to initiate the reporting of moving entities.

evidence_cards.content: The page describes conditions under which correlation shall be rejected (e.g., decorrelation criteria met, OCC on Dropped TN with RV=0 or RV=1, different E/C, simulated vs live track conflict, both tracks locally derived real-time), and specifies that after acceptance of manual correlation, automatic decorrelation processing is suppressed for 5 minutes.

source_locations.location: paragraphs (2)-(4), sections b and c, and Note at bottom

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These rejection conditions and post-acceptance suppression rules represent system state constraints that must hold before a new correlation request can be initiated — thus they function as preconditions for the use case 'Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas' if it involves track correlation. However, since this use case does not involve track correlation per se (as defined in goal scope), these are not direct preconditions for THIS use case.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU has correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This condition is explicitly stated as a prerequisite for the C2 JU to assume R2 of an IU (Inactive/Limited status Interface Unit) in accordance with reporting rules.

evidence_cards.content: The position of a slaved point or area is established as Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 from the Related TN at the time of the report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific data configuration required to initiate the definition of a slaved point/area, serving as a precondition for the system state.

evidence_cards.content: For moving points, lines, and areas (non-slaved), the Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word must be set to other than No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the necessary input values that must exist before defining non-slaved moving entities.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is the subject of a current engagement status message; i.e., the TN is the same TN appearing in a J10.2 Engagement Status message Target TN or Reference TN field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies a concrete operational contingency constraint (OCC) that must hold for a track before certain correlation actions can proceed — directly relevant to preconditions for defining reference points/geometric areas tied to a Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message originated by or addressed to own unit or a J12.0 Mission Assignment message originated by own unit for which a reply is required and has not been transmitted or received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Another OCC condition that constrains system state prior to use case execution — indicates active command/mission context affecting track handling.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is currently a controlled track, i.e., a J10.5 Controlling Unit Report message has been transmitted or received.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines control status as a precondition — essential for determining whether a track can be used as a Related TN for slaved geometry definition.

evidence_cards.content: The TN is an active or inactive IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies identity unit status as a possible constraint on track eligibility — may affect whether it can serve as a Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: If either subject track is the Target TN in a J10.2 Engagement Status message originated by the unit attempting correlation, and that track has an ID of Unknown or Hostile, and the other subject track has an ID of Friend, then automatic correlation may be allowed — with the Unknown/Hostile track being dropped.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an exception rule that modifies normal preconditions under specific ID conflict scenarios — critical for understanding when standard constraints are overridden during correlation attempts involving reference point definitions.

evidence_cards.content: The system must have a 'Related TN' (Track Number) established to which reference points or areas can be slaved.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: The definition of slaved points relies on establishing a position in relation to a Related TN; therefore, the existence of this entity is a prerequisite for defining slaved geometry.

evidence_cards.content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN, if Related TN does not already have the FT IND set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the existence of a 'Related TN' is a prerequisite condition for defining alerts on slaved points/areas, which relates to the preconditions for defining such geometric references in context.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data, when: a. A J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or b. A J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or c. A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, or d. The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section explicitly defines the triggering events (timeouts, specific message indicators, drop track messages, or quality thresholds) that cause the C² JU to initiate a reporting action for inactive units, which serves as the trigger evidence for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for defining slaved points and areas is the establishment of their position as Delta Latitude and 1/Delta Longitude from a Related TN at the time of the report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (setting the Slaved Indicator and establishing relative coordinates) that initiates the definition of slaved reference points and areas in relation to a Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific user action (operator action) required to initiate reporting on a previously reported emergency point or assume R² responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for defining the reference point (specifically a slaved Impact Point) is the identification of a specific ballistic missile track in the J3.0C5 Related Track Number field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific condition/event (relating to a track via TN) that initiates or defines the creation of the reference point in this context.

evidence_cards.content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN, as specified above, if Related TN does not already have the FT IND set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the triggering event for initiating an alert on a Related TN when a force tell alert is initiated on a slaved reference point or area, which directly relates to the trigger slot for defining reference points and geometric areas in relation to a Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU with R² for the Reference TN shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message upon receipt of a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2, Ballistic Missile Update Request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the specific event (receipt of a J7.1 message with ACT=2) that triggers the C2 JU's response behavior regarding reference point data updates, which is part of the overall use case flow.

evidence_cards.content: The J7.1 (ACT = 0) Data Update Request by Request Indicator message has the capability to request information by request indicator values, addressed to a specific Addressee TN(s) or collective address.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies another triggering mechanism (J7.1 ACT=0 message) that initiates the process of requesting and defining reference point data categories.

evidence_cards.content: Movement of the filter shall begin at the time of transmission of the J7.6 (ACT = 1) filter description report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the triggering event for the movement of a slaved filter: the transmission of the J7.6 message with ACT=1. This is the concrete action that initiates the use case behavior described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: The JU shall transmit a J3.5 message on the IU using the assigned address of the inactive IU when required for tactical situation reporting.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a specific message transmission (J3.5) triggered by the requirement for tactical situation reporting, which may relate to defining reference points in context.

evidence_cards.content: The position of a slaved point or area is established as Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 from the Related TN at the time of the report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the specific action/event that initiates the definition of the slaved point/area relative to the track: setting the Slaved Indicator to 1 and providing the delta coordinates in the report.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for decorrelation actions is the identification of a condition where local or remote data indicates that 'TN A' (the track in question) meets specific criteria such as being the subject of a pending J9.0 Command message, being controlled by own unit, or having been paired by own unit.

source_locations.location: Section c. Decorrelation Considerations, Paragraphs (2), (3), and (4)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This evidence establishes that the identification of the track's status (e.g., 'subject of a pending message', 'controlled', 'paired') acts as the operational trigger for the system to execute decorrelation logic, rather than just being a passive reporting state.

evidence_cards.content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN, as specified above, if Related TN does not already have the FT IND set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly links the initiation of an alert (trigger event) to the existence of a 'slaved reference point', which is defined by its relationship to a Related TN. This supports the causal link between field identification and the establishment of the reference point context.

evidence_cards.content: When the alert is terminated for the reference point or area, the JU terminating the alert shall also terminate the alert for Related TN, unless Related TN had the FT IND set prior to the slaved point or area alert being initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the termination logic dependent on the 'slaved point' status relative to the Related TN, reinforcing that the operational trigger (alert termination) acts upon the identified track/point structure.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for defining slaved points and areas is the establishment of a position (Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude) relative to a Related TN at the time of report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (setting Slaved Indicator = 1 with relative coordinates) that initiates the definition of the slaved reference point or area.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for defining a ballistic missile launch point is the derivation of the point via back azimuth from a missile track or by sensor detection of a launch.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (detection/derivation) that initiates the reporting and definition process for a reference point in relation to a track.

evidence_cards.content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN, as specified above, if Related TN does not already have the FT IND set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence describes the triggering event for defining/alerting on slaved points/areas in relation to a Related TN, which is the core action of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU defines slaved points and areas by establishing their position as Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 from the Related TN at the time of the report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This step describes the primary action for defining the reference point or area relative to the track number.

evidence_cards.content: To define a slaved square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse, the C2 JU sets the Square/Circle Switch field (value 1 for square/rectangle, value 2 for circle/ellipse) and ensures the Area Major Axis and Area Minor Axis fields are equal for squares/circles.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the data configuration required for geometric shapes within the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: For slaved ellipses, squares, and rectangles, the Axis Orientation shall change by an amount identical to the course change of the Related TN.

source_locations.location: Page 4-164, paragraph continuing from previous page

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This details the dynamic update rule for orientation during the definition process.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates that the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition in the main flow where automatic correlation is restricted, requiring operator intervention or parameter override.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition in the main flow where automatic correlation is restricted based on Mode II code discrepancies.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks (i.e., being updated with local positional data).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition in the main flow where automatic correlation is restricted for redundant local tracks.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1 (excluding 'No Statement').
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific condition in the main flow where automatic correlation is restricted based on track strength values.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for terminating a force tell alert on a track involves the JU with R² transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 3 or 4) message to terminate the alert and setting the appropriate EMG IND field or FT IND field in subsequent J3.2, J3.3, J3.4, or J3.5 messages to 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This details the specific step-by-step interaction sequence (main flow) for terminating an alert on a track, which is a key part of managing reference points and areas associated with tracks.

evidence_cards.content: An alternative method for clearing alerts is by reception of a J3.X message with the EMG IND and/or FT IND set to value 0.

source_locations.location: last sentence of paragraph under section 4.7.1.4.5

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an optional/alternative flow for clearing alerts, distinct from the primary J7.0 termination message flow.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU with R2 for the Reference TN shall respond with a J3.6 Space Track message upon receipt of a J7.1 message with the Data Update Request Action field set to value 2 (Ballistic Missile Update Request) on a specific TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary successful interaction sequence where the system responds to a request by transmitting data held in the appropriate word sequence.

evidence_cards.content: If an R2 shift occurs during execution of a DUR response, where the Number/Frequency of Updates field is set to value 2 or 3, the JU assuming R2 shall not respond to any prior Data Update Request.

source_locations.location: Section 4.7.2.1.6, last sentence of first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific condition within the main flow that alters the expected behavior (preventing response to prior requests).

evidence_cards.content: A single J3.0 message is used to define a segmented line with either 2 or 3 points.

source_locations.location: Page 4-160, paragraph 'a. Segmented Line and Multisided Area Definition'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the initial step in the main flow for creating geometric areas (segmented lines) using the J3.0 message format.

evidence_cards.content: Multiple J3.0 messages, each with a unique TN, are used to define segmented lines or multisided areas described by more than 3 points.

source_locations.location: Page 4-160, paragraph 'a. Segmented Line and Multisided Area Definition'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the extension of the main flow when the geometric area requires more than the standard number of points.

evidence_cards.content: When joining three or more points to form a segmented line, the segments are connected in sequence: the first segment is drawn from the point described in the Latitude and Longitude fields in the J3.0E0 word, to the point established by the Delta Latitude 1 and Delta Longitude 1 fields in the J3.0C1 word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exact construction logic (sequence of drawing) within the main flow for defining the geometry.

evidence_cards.content: To define a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse, the C2 JU uses a J3.0I/J3.0E0/J3.0C2 word sequence (or similar variants). The Point/Line/Area Descriptor in the J3.0I word is set to value 1 (Single Point Area). The Square/Circle Switch field indicates the shape type: value 1 for square/rectangle, and value 2 for circle/ellipse. If the Area Major Axis and Area Minor Axis fields are equal, a square or circle is described; if not equal, a rectangle or ellipse is described.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific data entry steps and parameter settings required to successfully create standard geometric areas.

evidence_cards.content: To define a slaved point or area, the C2 JU establishes the position as Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 from the Related TN at the time of the report and sets the Slaved Indicator to value 1. The presence or absence of the J3.0C4 continuation word determines if the slaving is relative (included) or true (excluded).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the core interaction steps for creating slaved reference points and areas relative to a track.

evidence_cards.content: To define a corridor or low level transit route (LLTR), the C2 JU reports using Point Type value 4, Line and Point Amplification value 3 (Corridor) or value 6 (Low Level Transit Route). Width is reported in the Area Major Axis, 4 field in the J3.0C5 word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific configuration steps for defining linear geographic areas like corridors.

evidence_cards.content: To define non-slaved moving points, lines, and areas, the C2 JU sets Course and Speed in the J3.0C2 word to values other than 'No Statement'. The system then extrapolates these entities based on the host's time of transfer to the terminal.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Outlines the procedure for defining dynamic, moving geographic references.

evidence_cards.content: When a JU ceases reporting a point, line, or area for which it had reporting responsibility, it shall transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message.

source_locations.location: Page 4-166, Section 4.4.3.6 'TERMINATION OF A POINT, LINE, OR AREA', first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the explicit system action required to terminate a defined reference point, line, or area, constituting a step in the main flow of managing these entities.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU fails to receive the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and further updates are not received, the JU may purge those points after a specified time period has elapsed with no updates.

source_locations.location: Page 4-167, Section 4.4.3.8 'PURGING OF EMERGENCY POINTS', second paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the system behavior regarding the removal of emergency points when normal termination signaling is absent, defining an alternative path within the management lifecycle.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU resolves conflicts between locally derived information and interface-reported data by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, using operator procedure, or via voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific interaction step (conflict resolution) within the main flow of managing track reporting procedures on the interface.

evidence_cards.content: To accomplish correlation, each C2 JU must continuously correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the continuous action required by the actor to maintain the state of reference points/areas relative to the interface data.

evidence_cards.content: A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN, as specified above, if Related TN does not already have the FT IND set.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a required step in the main flow when initiating alerts on slaved points/areas: propagate alert to Related TN unless already set.

evidence_cards.content: When the alert is terminated for the reference point or area, the JU terminating the alert shall also terminate the alert for Related TN, unless Related TN had the FT IND set prior to the slaved point or area alert being initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a required step in the main flow when terminating alerts on slaved points/areas: propagate termination to Related TN unless it was pre-set.

evidence_cards.content: A JU terminating a force tell alert on a track shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area that is slaved to the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a required step in the main flow when terminating alerts on tracks: propagate termination to all slaved reference points/areas.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU defines a slaved point or area by establishing its position as Delta Latitude and 1/Delta Longitude from the Related TN at the time of report when the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core action step for creating slaved points/areas in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the J3.0E0 word is included in a report of a slaved point or area, Latitude (0.0103 Minute) and Longitude (0.0103 Minute) shall be set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies data field constraints required during the definition process.

evidence_cards.content: When a square, rectangle, circle, or ellipse is slaved, the position established by Delta Latitude and 1/Delta Longitude represents the center of that area.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies the geometric interpretation of the defined position for specific area types.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.0 Reference Point message with the point type field set to value 7 (ASW) or value 8 (ASW, 1) is used to report ASW points, lines, or areas.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.5.2.3 REPORTING ASW POINTS, LINES, AND AREAS

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system action (reporting via J3.0 message) for defining reference points and geometric areas in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: ASW point amplification types are reported to provide a position or approximate location of a possible target of interest when no sensor measurement of course/speed is available for reporting in a J3.4 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the context and purpose of the main flow action for reporting these specific types of points.

evidence_cards.content: To report the actual or expected Launch Point of a ballistic missile, the C2 JU uses the J3.0 Reference Point message, deriving the point via back azimuth or sensor detection, and reports the launch time with the Time Function field set to value 4 (Departure Time).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action and message format for creating a Launch Point reference.

evidence_cards.content: If a missile launch point is related to a specific ballistic missile track, it shall be identified in the J3.0C5 Related 2 Track Number field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory step to relate the defined reference point to the Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: If the actual launcher is associated with a launch point, it shall be associated using the J7.7 Association message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an additional association step in the flow if the launcher is detected.

evidence_cards.content: To report the actual or expected Impact Point, the C2 JU uses the J3.0 Reference Point message, reporting the warhead type in the J3.0C5 Space Amplification field and the impact time with the Time Function field set to value 3 (Arrival Time).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action and message format for creating an Impact Point reference.

evidence_cards.content: If the Impact Point is related to a specific ballistic missile track, it shall be identified in the J3.0C5 Related 2 Track Number field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the mandatory step to relate the defined Impact Point to the Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: The main flow for defining slaved reference points and areas includes: (1) A JU initiating a force tell alert on a slaved reference point or area shall also initiate an alert on the Related TN if it does not already have the FT IND set; (2) When terminating the alert for the reference point or area, the JU shall also terminate the alert for the Related TN unless the Related TN had the FT IND set prior to initiation; (3) Terminating a force tell alert on a track shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area slaved to that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the canonical interaction sequence between C2 JU and system when managing alerts in context of slaved reference points/areas — directly informs the step-by-step normal flow of operations tied to the use case’s goal.

evidence_cards.content: If the filter is slaved to an existing TN, the TN shall be reported as TN, Related with Course and Speed set to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific step in the main flow for defining slaved reference points/geometric areas (filter definition) by specifying how the system reports the relationship to the Related TN.

evidence_cards.content: If Latitude and Longitude in the J7.6E0 are set to No Statement, then the position of TN, Related shall be used instead of the J7.6E0 Latitude and Longitude.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the conditional logic within the main flow where the system determines the geographic position based on input parameters when defining a slaved filter.

evidence_cards.content: Movement of the filter shall begin at the time of transmission of the J7.6 (ACT = 1) filter description report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the timing and action that concludes or advances the main flow sequence for establishing a moving/slaved filter.

evidence_cards.content: An exception to the rule against changing Point Amplification values while retaining a Reference TN allows a 'No Statement' value to be changed to a non-'No Statement' value.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a legal alternative path for modifying reference point attributes that diverges from the standard constraint of immutability.

evidence_cards.content: When an altitude range is reported, both Altitude, 100 Ft 1 and Altitude, 100 Ft 2 are used; specifically, if reporting at or below 10,000 feet, Altitude, 100 Ft 1 is set to 0 and Altitude, 100 Ft 2 is set to 100 (representing 10,000 Feet).

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow for altitude reporting where a range is defined rather than a single point.

evidence_cards.content: To relate or associate an ASW AOP (Point Type = 7 and Point Amplification = 12) to a track or point instead of slaving it, a J7.7 Association message may be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a valid alternative path for defining the relationship between an area and a track/point without using the standard slaving mechanism defined in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: When a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix shall be used for the new AOP, rather than assigning a new TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a legal alternative path in the main flow where instead of generating a new Track Number (TN) for a derived Area of Probability (AOP), the system reuses the existing TN from the source fix, diverging from the standard rule of assigning a new TN for derived reports.

evidence_cards.content: When the alert is terminated for the reference point or area (slaved point), the JU terminating the alert shall also terminate the alert for Related TN, unless Related TN had the FT IND set prior to the slaved point or area alert being initiated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific alternative flow for terminating alerts on slaved points where the termination propagates to the Related TN, diverging from the standard behavior of only terminating the local alert.

evidence_cards.content: A JU terminating a force tell alert on a track shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area that is slaved to the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where terminating an alert on a master track triggers the automatic termination of alerts on all associated slaved reference points/areas.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where a successful correlation leads to retaining the external track (PPLI source) and dropping the local surveillance track, diverging from a main flow that might retain local data.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C2 JU has R2 and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow handling duplicate Track Numbers, specifying conditions under which PPLI data overrides J3 data or vice versa based on quality flags.

evidence_cards.content: A Point Amplification value of No Statement may be changed to a non-No Statement value and retain the same Reference TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit exception to the rule prohibiting changes to Point Type/Amplification while retaining the same Reference TN; it represents a legal alternative path for modifying reference point attributes without changing identity.

evidence_cards.content: ASW Areas of Probability (AOP) reported in a J3.0 message with Point Type = 7 and Point Amplification = 12 shall not be slaved.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an alternative flow because it defines a specific category of reference point (AOP) that diverges from the main slaving process by explicitly prohibiting slaving, requiring a different association method instead.

evidence_cards.content: To relate or associate an ASW AOP to a track or point for which contact has been lost, a J7.7 Association message may be transmitted.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the successful recovery path for the non-slaved AOP case, providing the alternative mechanism to achieve the goal when standard slaving is prohibited.

evidence_cards.content: When a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix shall be used for the new AOP, diverging from the standard rule that requires assigning a new TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific alternative flow where the track number assignment logic differs from the main requirement (assigning a new TN) to preserve continuity when converting a fix to an AOP.

evidence_cards.content: J3.7 messages transmitted by nonR² JUs with the Response Indicator set to value 1 shall not affect reporting responsibility, providing an exception to the general retention of responsibility rules.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an alternative condition under which the primary actor's reporting responsibility is not affected, contrasting with the main flow rule that the originating unit always retains responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity (e.g., using a Reference TN used for a reference/emergency point for another entity type), except in the normal course of TN reuse.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition where changing the type of a reference point is prohibited/illegal.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change the Point Type and/or Point Amplification value of a reference point while retaining the same Reference TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a constraint preventing modification of specific fields for existing reference points without changing the TN.

evidence_cards.content: If an ASW Area of Probability (AOP) is reported in a J3.0 message with Point Type = 7 and Point Amplification = 12, it shall not be slaved.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific exception to the general rule that reference points and areas can be slaved to a Related TN. It explicitly prevents the slaving mechanism for this specific type of area.

evidence_cards.content: Emergency alerts are not used on reference points, lines, or areas.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the EW Filter Indicator is set, then all EW Fixes within/out the area, all EW AOPs having their center within/out the area, and all EW LOBs with origin within/out the area are filtered.

evidence_cards.content: If a Geographic Area Filter is set and the Reference Point Filter Indicator is set, then all points within/out the area, all lines with all points within/out the area, and all areas completely within/out the area are filtered.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific filtering logic (a constraint/exception to standard reporting) triggered by the combination of Geographic Area and Reference Point Filter indicators.

evidence_cards.content: If a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, the C² JU shall assume R² of the IU in accordance with reporting rules for a real-time track.

evidence_cards.content: If a J2 PPLI message (other than J2.0) is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, the C² JU shall assume R² of the IU.

evidence_cards.content: If a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, the C² JU shall assume R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow trigger based on an explicit 'Drop Track' command from another unit.

evidence_cards.content: If the Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0, the C² JU shall assume R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception flow trigger based on invalid or zero-quality position data, which is critical when defining reference points.

evidence_cards.content: When assuming R² of an IU under these exception conditions, the C² JU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG with Identity reported as Friend, and Track Number/Platform values from previous PPLI messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system response and alternative reporting behavior (exception flow outcome) triggered by the identified error conditions.

evidence_cards.content: When a system receives a No Statement value for a field which has a Reset to No Statement value and for which a value other than No Statement is locally held, the locally held value shall be retained regardless of whether it was locally or remotely derived.

evidence_cards.content: When a system receives a Reset to No Statement value, it shall automatically revert the locally held value of that field to No Statement.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the exception handling behavior (resetting state) when receiving a specific 'Reset to No Statement' command.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity; i.e., the Reference TN used to identify a particular reference or emergency point shall not be used for any other type of entity reported on the interface except in the normal course of TN reuse.

evidence_cards.content: As an exception to this rule a Point Amplification value of No Statement may be changed to a non-No Statement value and retain the same Reference TN.

evidence_cards.content: A change of positional information for a point, line, or area with independent course and speed does not constitute a change of data for the purpose of setting the Periodic Report Indicator to value 1.

evidence_cards.content: It is illegal to assume reporting responsibility for another unit's J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report.

evidence_cards.content: Each unit initiating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report shall assign a TN not known to be in use on the interface even if it is believed that such a report may concern the same emitter currently being reported in another J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report by another unit.

evidence_cards.content: The exception is a unit originating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report on a Fix, AOP, or LOB currently reported by the same unit or received from another unit in a J14.0 message shall assign the same TN, Reference in the J3.7 message as contained in the J14.0 message.

evidence_cards.content: If an illegal Environment/Category change is specified (marked 'X' in the table), the data shall be rejected if received.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful definition of a slaved filter, the movement of the filter begins at the time of transmission of the J7.6 (ACT = 1) filter description report.

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful definition of a slaved point or area, the position is established as Delta Latitude/Delta Longitude from the Related TN at the time of the report, and the Slaved Indicator is set to value 1.

evidence_cards.content: For slaved ellipses, squares, and rectangles, the Axis Orientation changes by an amount identical to the course change of the Related TN (-180 degrees if exceeding 179 degrees).

evidence_cards.content: Upon successful correlation of a Dropped TN to a Retained TN, the system state is updated such that specific data fields from the Dropped TN are transferred to the Retained TN. This includes Kinematic Data (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, etc.), Identification Data (ID/IAD, Platform, Activity, Type) subject to conflict restrictions, IFF/SIF Data, and Force Tell/Emergency Indicators.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the observable system state changes (data transfer and field updates) resulting from the successful completion of track correlation, which serves as evidence for postconditions regarding system state after definition.

evidence_cards.content: After successful definition of a slaved reference point or area, the system state includes that the Related TN has been alerted if it did not already have the FT IND set; and upon termination of the alert for the slaved point/area, the alert for the Related TN is also terminated unless the Related TN had the FT IND set prior to initiation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes observable system state changes in receiving units (JU) after successful completion of defining and managing alerts on slaved points/areas — directly addresses 'observable_result_in_receiving_unit' and 'persistence_of_slaved_relationship' aspects of postconditions.

evidence_cards.content: A JU terminating a force tell alert on a track shall also terminate the force tell alert on any reference point or area that is slaved to the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies propagation behavior upon termination — confirms that slaved relationships are maintained and acted upon during cleanup, supporting 'persistence_of_slaved_relationship' as part of postcondition state.

evidence_cards.content: After successful definition of a slaved filter, the system state includes: (1) The Slaved Indicator is set to value 1; (2) If slaved to an existing TN, that TN is reported as 'TN, Related' with Course and Speed set to 'No Statement'; (3) If Latitude/Longitude in J7.6E0 are 'No Statement', the position of 'TN, Related' is used instead; (4) If moving independently, 'TN, Related' is set to 'No Statement' with specified Course and Speed; (5) Movement begins at transmission time of the J7.6 (ACT = 1) filter description report.

evidence_cards.content: The slaved point or area center is plotted as the difference in Latitude and Longitude from the position of Related TN at the time of the report, regardless of whether slaved true or relative.
